sentences.cn_text: 只需读一首诗。
sentences.en_text: And just read a single poem.

sentences.cn_text: 在牛津讲座中，谢默斯·希尼认为，一首诗描绘了现实图景，呈现一种「瞥见的另类可能」，以或大或小的方式与读者自身的现实形成矛盾对照。
sentences.en_text: In his Oxford lectures, Seamus Heaney argued that a poem draws a picture of reality, a “glimpsed alternative” that sets up a contradiction with your own, in ways little and large.

sentences.cn_text: 你与诗之间的协商，正是问题的核心所在。
sentences.en_text: The negotiation, between you and it, is the heart of the matter.

sentences.cn_text: 诗人看到了什么是你未曾看到的？
sentences.en_text: What does the poet see that you don’t?

sentences.cn_text: 这种差异意味着什么？
sentences.en_text: What does the difference mean?

sentences.cn_text: 这可能是你有过的最好的对话之一。
sentences.en_text: It could be one of the best conversations you ever have.

sentences.cn_text: 忘掉自助类书籍；阅读本身就是实践中的自助。
sentences.en_text: Forget self-help books; reading is self-help in action.

sentences.cn_text: 但大多数情况下，商界并非如此。
sentences.en_text: But for the most part, this isn’t what the business community does.

sentences.cn_text: 我至今未曾遇到一位有规律阅读习惯的首席执行官。
sentences.en_text: I have yet to meet a chief executive who reads regularly.

sentences.cn_text: 许多人跳过报纸，而杂志则更难触及。
sentences.en_text: Many skip newspapers, and magazines are a stretch.

sentences.cn_text: 他们说自己没有时间。
sentences.en_text: They don’t have time, they say.

sentences.cn_text: 阅读效率低下；他们可以从周围的人那里获得所需信息。
sentences.en_text: It’s inefficient; they can get the information they need from those around them.

sentences.cn_text: 必要时，他们可能会在长途飞行前拿起一本商业书籍，希望它像食谱一样提供万无一失的配方。
sentences.en_text: At a pinch, they might pick up a business book before a long flight, in the hope that, like a cookbook, it will provide a foolproof recipe.

sentences.cn_text: 有些人被我称之为「商业车祸」类书籍吸引——讲述Theranos、普渡制药或WeWork的故事。
sentences.en_text: Some are drawn to what I think of as “business car crash” books — the stories of Theranos, Purdue, or WeWork.

sentences.cn_text: 但在这些狭窄的兴趣池之外，还有一片浩瀚的海洋在等待，其中充满了酝酿的思想、精神探险和想象力的更新。
sentences.en_text: But outside those narrow pools of interest, a vast ocean awaits, bountiful with simmering ideas, mental adventure and imaginative refreshment.

sentences.cn_text: 神经科学家一直努力证明，书籍带来的愉悦不是放纵，而是对你有益。
sentences.en_text: Neuroscientists have been at pains to demonstrate that the pleasure a book provides isn’t indulgence; it’s good for you.

sentences.cn_text: 阅读不仅能让你更好地了解世界，还能改善我们被科技侵蚀的专注能力。
sentences.en_text: Reading will keep you better informed about the world but it can also improve our tech-shattered ability to concentrate.

sentences.cn_text: 站在他人立场能够微调我们的社会理解能力，这在我们努力理解朋友、邻居、客户和同事时大有裨益。
sentences.en_text: Standing in the shoes of others fine tunes our social understanding, useful as we struggle to understand friends, neighbours, customers and co-workers.

sentences.cn_text: 当我们模拟场景、人物和心理状态时，大脑的不同部分会参与其中。
sentences.en_text: Different parts of our brain engage as we simulate scenes, characters and mental states.

sentences.cn_text: 我们的想象力——还记得吗？
sentences.en_text: Our imagination — remember that?

sentences.cn_text: ——被重新点燃了。
sentences.en_text: — is rekindled.

sentences.cn_text: 毫无疑问，只工作不玩耍确实会让杰克或吉尔变得乏味。
sentences.en_text: It is undoubtedly true that all work and no play really does make Jack, or Jill, dull.

sentences.cn_text: 解药就在手边。
sentences.en_text: The cure is right at hand.

sentences.cn_text: 阅读既廉价又简单，最重要的是，它充满乐趣。
sentences.en_text: Reading is cheap, easy and, most important, it’s fun.

sentences.cn_text: 今年就释放你的想象力吧。
sentences.en_text: Liberate your imagination this year.

sentences.cn_text: 我们正处于科学写作的黄金时代，这些作品如此清晰易懂，即便是普通读者也能领略发现的不可预测性之乐。
sentences.en_text: We are living through a golden age of science writing, so lucid and accessible that even lay readers can relish the unpredictability of discovery.

sentences.cn_text: 被不确定性困扰？
sentences.en_text: Daunted by uncertainty?

sentences.cn_text: 站在科学家的立场上，见证突破在多大程度上源于偶然、冲突和纯粹的精神毅力。
sentences.en_text: Stand in the shoes of scientists and witness the degree to which breakthroughs emerge from accidents, conflict and sheer mental stamina.

sentences.cn_text: 「我们从未对任何事情确信无疑，」物理学家（兼作家）卡洛·罗韦利说。
sentences.en_text: “We are never sure of anything,” says the physicist (and writer) Carlo Rovelli.

sentences.cn_text: 你不需要多外出。
sentences.en_text: You don’t need to get out more.

sentences.cn_text: 如果你像大多数商界人士一样，生活在办公室、飞机、火车、家、会议室和洗手间之间奔波，那么你真正需要做的是多待在室内，坐下来——读一本书。
sentences.en_text: If, like most business people, you spend your life dashing from office to plane, train to home, boardroom to washroom, what you really need to do is stay in more, sit down — and read a book.

sentences.cn_text: 研究还发现，阅读能让我们更乐于助人，减少偏见，甚至延长寿命——如果手中有一本好书，我们将更加享受这一切。
sentences.en_text: Reading has also been found to make us more helpful, to reduce bias, and even to increase longevity — something we will enjoy all the more if we have a good book in our hands.

sentences.cn_text: （是的，所有这些益处与实体书的关联都比电子书更紧密。）
sentences.en_text: (And yes, all these benefits are more closely associated with physical books than digital ones.)

sentences.cn_text: 阅读小说。
sentences.en_text: Read fiction.

sentences.cn_text: 任何小说。
sentences.en_text: Any fiction.

sentences.cn_text: 摆脱算法束缚，自由选择——任何作品。
sentences.en_text: Free yourself from algorithms and choose — anything.

sentences.cn_text: 你不需要技术来获得沉浸式体验——只需投身于跨越时空的叙事之中。
sentences.en_text: You don’t need technology for an immersive experience — just surrender to narratives across time and place.

sentences.cn_text: 现代的（塞巴斯蒂安·巴里或奥尔加·托卡尔丘克）、经典的（弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫或詹姆斯·鲍德温）或类型的（斯蒂芬·金、玛格丽特·阿特伍德、乔治·西默农）——都无关紧要。
sentences.en_text: Modern (Sebastian Barry or Olga Tokarczuk), classic (Virginia Woolf or James Baldwin) or genre (Stephen King, Margaret Atwood, Georges Simenon) — it doesn’t matter.

sentences.cn_text: 小说邀请你在他人的生活中不为人知地流连。
sentences.en_text: Fiction invites you to loiter unseen in the lives of others.

sentences.cn_text: 我们也正处于翻译的黄金时代，因此你可以前往任何时间或地点。
sentences.en_text: We are living through a golden age of translation too, so you can go anywhere in time or place.
